sections.content: How many people are "purchasing managers and directors"?

36,785 people

were counted on the census as "purchasing managers and directors" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Purchasing managers and directors (not retail) organise and co-ordinate the purchasing functions of industrial, commercial, government organisations and public agencies to ensure cost-effectiveness.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 45 to 49 years. Of the whole working population 11% were aged 45 to 49 years. For people working as "purchasing managers and directors", 15.7% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "purchasing managers and directors" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "purchasing managers and directors" included:

  • financial managers and directors
  • marketing, sales and advertising directors
  • education managers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "purchasing managers and directors" there were more men than women (60.5% compared with 39.5%).

This means "purchasing managers and directors" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "corporate managers and directors".

Men made up 60.5% and women made up 39.5% of "purchasing managers and directors"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "purchasing managers and directors" included:

  • graphic and multimedia designers
  • leisure and sports managers and proprietors
  • transport and distribution clerks and assistants

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "purchasing managers and directors" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "purchasing managers and directors" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "purchasing managers and directors", 6.5% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (93.5% compared with 6.5%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (97.1%) than self-employed (2.9%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
